Method of Attack: Phishing emails impersonating HR staff with links to archives stored on public cloud storage services
Payloads delivered via LNK (shortcuts) and XLAM (Excel Macro-Enabled add-on) files
Attacker-controlled cloud storage set up as network drive to launch malware
Replacement of JPG, PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS, XLSX files on network drives with malicious LNKs to propagate attack
Use of LaZagne open-source tool (obfuscated with PyArmor) to steal credentials from memory and web browsers
PowerShell scripts for command and control, deploying phishing windows impersonating Microsoft Outlook, analyzing and uploading documents to cloud storages
Lateral movement inside victim network over 2 to 6 months
Impacted Systems: Corporate networks in construction, consulting, financial, retail, tourism, legal, and insurance sectors
Systems in Russia, Ukraine, United Kingdom, Norway, Germany, Canada
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with malicious attachments or links

Public cloud storage services (Dropbox, cloudme.com, koofr.net, pcloud.com, idata.uz, drivehq.com, driveonweb.de, opendrive.com, powerfolder.com, docs.live.net, syncwerk.cloud, cloud.woelkli.com, framagenda.org)
MultCloud platform for managing cloud storage and command and control
Indicators of Compromise: Use of multiple public cloud storage domains listed above
Replacement of common document and image files with malicious shortcuts
Phishing emails impersonating company HR with official logos and company domain in sender address
